title: Show hidden files in Finder with Command+Shift+Period
summary: Finder hides files and folders whose names start with a dot, such as configuration files. Press Command+Shift+Period in a Finder window to show or hide them.

aliases.text: как увидеть скрытые файлы в finder

prerequisites: A Finder window is open and active

steps.explain: Click a Finder window to make it active, then press Command+Shift+Period (the period key next to the comma). Dotted files and folders appear dimmed. Press the same keys again to hide them.
steps.gui: In a Finder window, press Command (⌘) + Shift (⇧) + Period (.). Press it again to hide hidden files.
steps.expect: Files whose names start with a dot, such as .zshrc, appear in the folder with a dimmed look.

alternatives.explain: Terminal method: turn on hidden files in Finder and keep the setting after a restart. Finder restarts, so save your work and close Finder windows first.
alternatives.cmd: defaults write com.apple.finder AppleShowAllFiles -bool true && killall Finder

verify.expect: Prints 1 when hidden files are shown and 0 when they are hidden. An error about a missing default means the setting was never changed.

warnings: The Terminal method restarts Finder. Finder windows close and Finder reopens by itself; save your work first.
Hidden files are hidden for a reason. Do not delete or move files whose names you do not recognize.

rollback.explain: Undo the Terminal method: hide hidden files again and restart Finder.
rollback.cmd: defaults write com.apple.finder AppleShowAllFiles -bool false && killall Finder

rollback.explain: Or press Command+Shift+Period again in a Finder window to hide hidden files for the current view.
rollback.gui: In a Finder window, press Command (⌘) + Shift (⇧) + Period (.).

source.title: defaults manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
